messages.subject: setup a new environment
parts:
Dear all,

I have two questions regarding packrat. The first one is regarding setting up a new environment with specific package versions. I have read and understood how to bootstrap a new project/environment/directory from an existing packrat.lock file but I wonder how I could generate one non-interactively. In Python, for example, I could do this with pip from a plain text file: "pip install -r requirements.txt" where the text file consists of lines like "numpy=='1.9.1'" or "matplotlib>='1.3'". Is something like this possible?

And then more generally, is it possible to interact with packrat functions from the command line directly? Is anything like that planned?

I ask all this because I want to manage R environments from a web application. So doing all this from an interactive R session is possible but seems a lot more involved. I suppose, I could write stand-alone scripts myself but you guys certainly have a lot more experience.

Thank you for your opinions,
Moritz
